title: Part 2
html:
Katwa: the sannyasa. Shantipur. Burdwan and Shashimukhi. On through Medinipur and Narayangarh (pp. 21–40)

[p. 21]

217Only the longing of love remains —
thus I have shown you where love is to be found.

218Now strive with all your heart for love:
you will be fulfilled, and the torments of worldly life will go.

219Through quarrels, disputes, hatred and lies
worldly life becomes a hell — think on this.

220For money the householder tells lies,
cheats, and even kills wherever he can.

221What more can I say of the householder's rotten life?
He is worn out by sons, daughters, possessions and wealth.

222You never think whose you are and who is yours;
for the sake of an inert lump of flesh you are busy earning.

223Death will surely come, there are no two ways about it,
yet you keep thinking you will live forever.

224However many shastras you have read, combing every detail,
by reading you have all become nothing but great fools.

225The more learning and cleverness, the more selfishness;
the more you read, the dirtier the heart becomes.

226With your lips you call another's wife "mother",
but find her alone and at once you are blinded by lust.

227Lust and anger are enemies when it comes to others,
but when it comes to yourself they are your friends.

[p. 22]

228All these are the boundless torments of hell;
think about it in your heart, even once.

229Until devotion to God arises,
so long will you remain in such a hell.

230A small self-interest you can give up,
but millions of coins can lead you astray.

231For the people of Kali the essence is the Name of Hari alone;
take that Name and go to the eternal abode.

232Always say "Hari bol!" with thrilling joy;
why make such a commotion in the bazaar of Kali?

233What difference is there between a mansion and a hut?
Go and ask the learned, brothers.

234As a king sleeps on a bedstead in his palace,
so the poor man sleeps in his hut.

235The king drinks water from a golden cup,
the hut-dweller drinks from an earthen pot.

236The aim of both is the same — to quench thirst;
the king's golden cup is mere illusion.

237Does the king eat dal of pearls and curry of gems?
Does he cook his rice out of diamonds?

238Drunk with pride, the king cannot see it,
and so he comes and goes again and again."

[p. 23]

239Thus Chaitanya Gosai taught,
and great crowds gathered in one place.

240Seated beneath a bilva tree in Kantaka-nagara,
he gave many teachings in a loud voice.

241The words of his holy mouth are the essence of Vedanta;
whoever hears them is freed from worldly existence.

242Thus a day and a night went by.
The next morning the Lord bathed.

243The women wept, pressing the ends of their saris to their eyes,
their tears pouring down in torrents.

244One said: "May every misfortune that threatens such beauty fall on me!1
How will his mother stay alive?

245Here the pride of millions of Cupids is humbled;
never have I seen such beautiful hair.

246How lovely is his spotless chin!
His lotus eyes outshine the blue lotus.

247Never have I seen such a wondrous form.
How will Nimai bear the kaupina and the staff?

248Keshava Thakura2 must be made of stone —
how can he shave off his hair? How cruel!

249Ah, how beautiful is the garland of forest flowers at his throat!
The radiance of his face has lit up every direction."

[p. 24]

250So the women said many things.
Meanwhile the Lord quietly called me.

251The Lord said, "Quickly bring all the things that are needed;
I shall shave my head to take sannyasa.

252I will no longer stay at home in bondage;
at home there is the torment of hell at every turn."

253Hearing this, pure-hearted Gadadhara,
the Avadhuta Nityananda and Chandrashekhara

254brought all the requisites fit for sannyasa
and filled the sannyasi's store.

255They called a barber named Deva,
and the barber sat down beneath the bilva tree.

256Then Chaitanya Gosai said to the barber,
"Shave me, Deva — I am going to Vraja."

257Receiving Bharati's order, the barber
sat down close by to shave him.

258When at last the barber put the razor to his hair,
the women all cried out at once.

259The women said, "Barber, do not do this!
Do not shave off such locks of hair!"

260So saying, the women burst into tears,
and then Deva began to shave.

[p. 25]

261Thousands upon thousands of people
came flocking to Kantaka-nagara to see the sannyasa.

262At the close of day, his head shaved,
Nimai put on the dress of a sannyasi.

263Staff and water-pot in hand, he put on the kaupina
and covered it with saffron cloth.

264Gosai stood before Bharati,
lighting up every quarter with his beauty — I would give my life for him!

265The Avadhuta, Gadadhara and Gangadasa
one by one stood beside the sannyasi.

266Seeing the Lord's wondrous form, Bharati
bowed inwardly at his lotus feet.

267Inwardly he said, "Gosai, you are God himself;
the whole universe, moving and unmoving, is under you.

268To teach the people you have put on the kaupina;
to show the path of bhakti you have made yourself subject to the lowly."

269In the afternoon the Lord became a sannyasi,
and the women raised the ulu-cry.3

270Creepers, leaves, branches and trees floated in love;
beasts, birds and insects seemed to break into dance.

271Hundreds of thousands showered flowers,
and Kantaka-nagara became the Nandana garden.4

[p. 26]

272Bharati gave him the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
Hundreds of thousands came and went.

273The respectable married women, filling their palms,
showered puffed rice on the Lord's head.

274The cry of "Hari!" rose, piercing the sky,
and all rolled on the ground, steeped in devotion.

275The Name, bursting through the heavens, wandered the skies,
and all the gods listened, drunk with joy.

276That night my Lord stayed awake
and passed the night dancing with the Name of Hari.

277In the morning the Lord said to Shekhara:
"All of you go home to Nadia.

278Go with Brahmananda to my mother
and tell her that Nimai has taken sannyasa.

279If my mother weeps,
comfort her with words of reassurance."

280Then, with Nityananda and Gadadhara,
he took Bharati and set out in high spirits.

281I followed behind, carrying the wooden sandals.
Chaitanya Gosai was drunk with the wine of the Name.

282Hundreds of thousands followed the Lord,
and many pandits went along to see him.

[p. 27]

283Rudradeva, Ramaratna, Jagai Pandita,
Gangadasa, Shambhuchandra, famed in the world,

284Ishana, Shankara, Balarama, Gadadhara,
Chanda-Chandeshvara, crest-jewel of pandits,

285Kashishvara, Nyayaratna and Siddheshvara,
Panchanana the Vedantist and Ratnakara —

286all these great pandits went with him,
while Sri Krishna Chaitanya, drunk with love, went on in delight.

287Absorbed in dance, the Lord ran ahead —
now running, now leaping, now falling to the ground.

288Tears streamed from his eyes,
and Bharati Gosai wept, tasting that love.

289Then, in ecstasy, he went eastwards
and hurried, drunk with feeling, to the Acharya's house.5

290He stayed some time in the Acharya's house,
and meanwhile Mother Shachi came there too.

291Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu bowed
at his mother's feet and spoke to her tenderly.

292After a few words, cutting through the bonds of affection,
he set out southwards, leaving everyone.

293Ishana, Pratapa, Gangadasa, Gadadhara
and Baneshvara went along with the sannyasi.

[p. 28]

294When we all reached Burdwan,
I began to wonder what fate had in store for me.

295Looking at me, the Lord began to speak,
as if streams of nectar were flowing out.

296Clapping me on the back, the Lord said,
"Come, Govinda, let us go to your house."

297Hearing this, I started,
and the Lord, laughing, walked on with a swaying gait.

298"When the Lord took sannyasa, I put on the kaupina,
gave up pride and became utterly humble.

299I have no more desire to live a household life;
I will go with the Lord, dancing."

300As we walked along, I folded my hands
and said a few words in reply:

301"I will not go back to Kanchananagar, Lord;
I have given up vile household life like excrement."

302While I was saying this, my wife,
having somehow heard of it, came there in haste.

303Tears were streaming from her eyes,
and she threw herself down at my feet.

304With tears she began to say:
"Come back home, I will go with you.

[p. 29]

305Over a trifle you have abandoned the household —
tell me, what provision have you made for your maidservant?

306To whose door shall I go, where shall I beg?
Who will give me alms out of kindness?

307What is in store for me? At whose door
shall I go begging for my belly's sake?"

308Hearing her words, I hung my head
and inwardly kept saying, "Hari, Hari."

309Remembering Hari cuts all bonds;
that is why I fixed my mind on Hari's feet.

310Then merciful Chaitanya, seeing this,
began to speak to her sweet words.

311Hearing the Lord's words, the unhappy woman
began to wet the earth with her tears.

312Distraught with weeping, she looked about her on all sides,
while the Lord tried to make her understand, speaking of the highest truth.

313Hearing those words of the Lord so suddenly,
she covered her eyes with the end of her sari and wept.

314Her weeping moved the Lord to compassion,
and at once he turned to me and said:

315"Govinda, you stay at home;
I will go to Puri with another servant."

[p. 30]

316At these words tears poured from my eyes,
and at once I fell, distraught, clasping his feet.

317I washed his two feet with my tears,
and at once the Lord turned and went on.

318Then my neighbours gathered together
and began to talk to me, trying to win me over.

319But I began to speak of the poison of worldly life
and to expound the hidden nature of woman:

320"Listen, brothers, to what I say of woman:
the woman and her lover are one and the same life.

321If now you all turn your gaze to the portion of the Self,
you will see that woman and lover are all one.

322Those who, thinking it sweeter than nectar,
drink a woman's spittle with their eyes closed,

323forgetting eternal bliss and delighting in that —
shame on such a wretch; his birth is wasted.

324My Gauranga is the complete Brahman, the eternal;
shall I abandon his company and take up household life?"

325Saying this, we crossed the Damodar
and went on to the house of Kashi Mitra.6

326Kashi Mitra is a virtuous man,
and the Lord went and stayed in his house.

[p. 31]

327For the offering Mitra gave good rice,
and the Lord, seeing the rice, praised it.

328The Lord said, "This rice is very fine.
By what name do people call it?"

329Mitra said, "Its name is Jagannatha-bhoga;
when it is offered, every wish is fulfilled."

330Hearing "Jagannatha-bhoga", the Lord started,
and at once streams of love began to flow.

331Weeping, he said, "Ah, Jagannatha!
Quickly draw me to you!"

332Having cooked greens, dal and various dishes,
the Lord, rejoicing, put them all together.

333The smell of the betho greens7 filled the air,
and before the offering was even made my mind was restless.

334The Lord said, "Quickly bring tulasi;
we will offer the bhoga and I will give you prasada to your heart's content.

335You are very hungry, my child;
that is why you keep looking this way and that."

336I was deeply ashamed at the Lord's words
and stood there with my head hung down.

337He made the offering and distributed the prasada,
and my heart rejoiced at the gravy of the shukta.

[p. 32]

338I happily ate half a fried bitter gourd,
lifting big mouthfuls into my mouth.

339Sour chutney8 with molasses — like nectar;
how much I ate, my face beaming with joy!

340In the afternoon Gora-chand left Mitra's house
and hastened southwards — a snare of love.

341In due course we reached the village of Hajipur,
and there the Lord intoxicated everyone with the Name of Hari.

342Outside the village is a huge banyan tree,
and there we slowly settled down.

343In the evening the Lord began sankirtana,
and the Name rose up into the sky, piercing the heavens.

344The Lord began to dance and intoxicated the whole countryside —
where were his kaupina and waist-string? His dress in disarray.

345Now he falls crashing to the ground,
now, foaming at the mouth, rolls this way and that.

346Hundreds of people gathered there,
and all became intoxicated with the sankirtana of the Name.

347All the men and women together grew drunk with the Name.
Blessed is the power of the Name — I would give my life for it!

348Boys and girls, old men, young men and young women
clapped their hands and danced with devotion.

[p. 33]

349Half the night passed in this way,
and then Hari cooked the rice received as alms.

350A village devotee brought ghee,
and with the ghee my Lord fried bitter gourd.

351Shukta with neem, ghee and fried bitter gourd —
my king of Nadia offered them as bhoga.

352Gora-Hari took only a little prasada,
and then I sat down with a leaf-plate.

353I ate the prasada puffing and panting,
[the second line of the couplet is missing in the edition]

354and when my belly swelled up,
I went and took refuge at the Lord's feet.

355Then the Lord passed his hand over my belly,
and at once it went back to normal.

356Then I raised the cry "Hari, Hari!",
and the devotees started up in surprise.

357Next morning beautiful Gauranga rose,
called the devotees and spoke with them at length.

358Having reasoned with the devotees, he took his leave
and set off quickly with his companions.

359When he drew near Medinipur,
people heard the news and came running.

[p. 34]

360Among them a rich man came up
and was struck dumb on seeing the Lord's form.

361His name was Keshava Samanta, a very wealthy man.
With much guile the rich man talked of many things.

362Now he would say with a laugh, "O best of sannyasis,
take some money, as much as your heart desires.

363Throw off the kaupina and put on proper clothes —
why should a young man take sannyasa?

364Enjoy yourself, yogi, by serving your senses;
why die a slave to renunciation?"

365Hearing the rich man's words, the Lord smiled slightly
and patiently set about teaching him.

366The Lord said, "Money, cowries, gold and emeralds
are all transformations of clay, as the shastras say.

367All that is a transformation of clay will in time become clay.
Why then do you all burst with pride?

368Do not set your feet in the snare of the Lord's maya,
or you will die again and again.

369Whoever wants to die again and again,
the bonds of maya will never let him go.

370Give up everything and worship Him with devotion;
then supreme bliss will arise in your heart.

[p. 35]

371You wander about saying 'mine, mine',
not knowing you have already entered the jaws of Time.

372When it grinds you between its teeth,
where will your beautiful women be then?

373Where will your gold, your silver and your grain be?
Where will your thickened milk, cream and curd-cheese be?

374This cherished body will burn to ashes,
and if it does not burn, jackals will eat it.

375Your head will roll in the filth by the leather-worker's door.9
Worship Krishna, say 'Krishna' — time is passing in vain.

376What are you proud of? Everything is transient.
The eternal reality is Krishna, the place where one finds peace.

377O best of rich men, listen to my words:
do you eat diamonds, pearls and emeralds?

378A handful of rice is enough to stop hunger;
why then are you proud all the time?"

379Having taught the rich man thus,
the Lord looked at me and said a few words:

380"[Let us go to Narayangarh,]10 let us go;
perhaps we shall find some joy there."

381Saying just this, he rose quickly,
and at once I lifted the sandals onto my shoulder.

[p. 36]

382While my Gora walked happily along the road,
in the evening we reached that place.

383In Narayangarh there is a Shiva, Dhaleshvara,
and he hurried to see him.

384He is the village deity of Narayangarh.
The Lord began to weep, his tears flowing in streams.

385Crying aloud, "Hara, Hara!",
the Lord fell crashing to the ground.

386Choked with love, he rolled on the ground,
and his cloth and water-pot fell who knows where.

387The great sattvika ecstasies11 arose in him,
and in his love blood spurted from his pores.

388His outer cloth and kaupina slipped off who knows where;
how many ascetics came there to see that state!

389Vanaprasthas, brahmacharis, so many renunciants
came there to see the Lord of Nadia.

390Seeing his love and devotion, all were amazed
and fell to the ground, crying, "He is a god!"

391Raising the cry of "Hari!", the Lord began to dance,
and seeing that tremendous state, all shuddered.

392Thus everyone was dancing beneath the tree.
[the second line of the couplet is missing in the edition]

[p. 37]

393I, a sinner and the lowest of men, kept eyeing the laddus,12
and was seized by a craving to eat my fill of them.

394The all-knowing Lord understood me by a hint,
and, making the laddus into prasada, gave them to me to eat.

395I ate five laddus and filled my belly,
and a brahmana brought me cool water.

396In time the villagers heard the news
and one by one gathered at that place.

397The Lord made the offering and distributed the prasada,
and all of them together received it there.

398Seeing their devotion to the prasada, I thought hard:
I, the glutton, had filled my belly before everyone else.

399Thinking this and repenting inwardly,
to destroy my sin I clasped the Lord's feet.

400He reasoned with me in many words and placed his foot on my head,
and at once the confusion left my mind.

401Then in ecstasy he began to dance,
and all grew drunk on the wine of the nectar of Hari.

402Some danced, some rolled on the ground,
some ran towards the trees crying "Krishna!"

403Gradually a great crowd gathered at that place.
[the second line of the couplet is missing in the edition]

[p. 38]

404Hearing of the new sannyasi,
everyone came to that place one after another.

405Vireshvara Sena and Bhavani Shankara
came before the Lord with many people.

406With palanquins, elephants, horses and many carriages
they came into the Lord's presence.

407Bhavani Shankara is a very rich man;
he came with hundreds of people.

408Kettle-drums on camels' backs, colourful banners,
four silver howdahs going on ahead.

409All of them worms of worldliness, drunk with pride;
seeing them, the Lord's heart filled with compassion.

410Seeing their condition, merciful Chaitanya
blessed them by giving them devotion.

411Teaching devotion, the Lord intoxicated them all,
and more than a hundred thousand listened, still as puppets.

412With a straw in his teeth and folded hands, the Lord said,
"All of you, listen to my humble words."

413The Lord said, "Listen, all you wealthy gentlemen:
this world is like a juggler's trick.

414When, overcome by sleep, you mount a throne,
then the thought 'I am king' arises in your mind.

[p. 39]

415Hundreds of ministers and friends deliberate,
hundreds of thousands of subjects come with gifts.

416But you never reflect on what all this is.
Fool, understand: it is the shadow of a reflection.

417The inert world is a reflection of the truth of Krishna,
and dream is a reflection of that — so say the Vedas.

418Think it over: both of them are dreams;
the only difference is sleeping or waking.

419All the king's kingdom is a waking dream.
Consider what is true and what is false by the word of the Vedas.

420Gold, silver, gems and pearls are transformations of clay;
the precious thing is Krishna — this is the essence.

421The eternal reality is Bhagavan, so say the Vedas,
and all else that you see is false.

422One who stays submerged under water —
how can he see the things on dry land?

423If you lift him out of the water onto the bank,
then he will see the things of the land close by.

424So it is with one who is sunk in worldliness —
how can he see Radha and Krishna?

425He over whose eyes the blinkers of maya are tied
is always blind, like the oil-mill bullock.

[p. 40]

426Who knows what lies inside a mountain cave?
How can one know its truth from outside?

427Just so the subtle nature of the inert world —
who can perceive it by gross means?

428The endless universes are the Lord's form;
he alone understands this who gives up the path of ritual works.

429When you give up inertness and become full of consciousness,
then you will be able to see Krishna's form.

430Listen: by Krishna's will power has been given to matter,
but only one who has devotion can see it.

431A knot has formed between matter and consciousness;
only one whose rajas and tamas are gone can untie it.13

432Who can understand the nature of the inert world?
People keep going round like the oil-presser's bullock.

433The oil-presser's bullock walks a short track, it is true,
but, caught in that plight, it never finds the end.

434Blinkered, it goes round one path until it dies;
just so the soul goes round within worldly life.

435Wearing the blinkers of maya, the soul goes round till it dies,
and therefore it cannot see the subtle truth.

436Coveting others' property and others' wives,
how can one then practise the worship of Krishna?

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. "To take on the misfortunes (balai)" is a Bengali formula of admiration: "may every evil that threatens this beauty fall on me".
  2. Keshava Bharati, Chaitanya's sannyasa guru.
  3. Ulu-dhvani, the ritual ululation of Bengali women at solemn moments.
  4. Nandana is Indra's heavenly garden.
  5. Advaita Acharya's house at Shantipur. Govinda passes very briefly over an episode known from other biographies: after his sannyasa Chaitanya spent several days at Shantipur, where Shachi came to see him.
  6. Kashi Mitra, not to be confused with Kashi Mishra of Puri. The Damodar river flows near Burdwan.
  7. Beto shak: bathua or white goosefoot, a popular Bengali leafy green.
  8. Chukra/chukai: a sour dish (a broth of sour leaves or fruit), sweetened with molasses.
  9. A harsh image from street speech: the dead body thrown out where the leather-workers (muchi) work.
  10. The line is corrupt in the edition ("…na chala mora jai"). From the context (the next page) Narayangarh is meant.
  11. The sattvika bhavas are the eight bodily signs of ecstasy: stupor, perspiration, hair standing on end, faltering voice, trembling, change of colour, tears and fainting.
  12. The lines before this, explaining where the laddus came from, are missing in the edition.
  13. Rajas and tamas, the gunas of passion and ignorance.
